info.o: Arcus zygomaticus
info.i: Tuberositas masseterica (lateral angle and ramus of the mandible)
info.f: Elevates the mandible – closes the jaw

info.o: Fossa temporalis and fascia temporalis
info.i: Processus coronoideus mandibulae
info.f: Elevates the mandible; posterior fibres retract it

parts: Superior head of lateral pterygoid muscle
Inferior head of lateral pterygoid muscle

info.o: Upper head: crista infratemporalis of the greater wing of the sphenoid · lower head: lateral surface of the lamina lateralis processus pterygoidei
info.i: Fovea pterygoidea of the condylar process and the articular disc of the TMJ
info.f: Pulls the mandible forward, opens the mouth, grinding movement to the opposite side

info.o: Fossa pterygoidea (medial side of the lamina lateralis) and tuber maxillae
info.i: Tuberositas pterygoidea (medial side of the mandibular angle)
info.f: Elevates and protrudes the mandible; forms a muscle sling with the masseter

info.o: Alveolar processes of maxilla and mandible (molar region) and raphe pterygomandibularis
info.i: Angulus oris, blends into M. orbicularis oris
info.f: Presses the cheek against the teeth (chewing, blowing)

info.o: Medial orbital margin and lig. palpebrale mediale
info.i: Runs in rings around the orbit; lateral palpebral raphe
info.n: N. facialis (VII) – rr. temporales and zygomatici
info.f: Closes the eyelids (palpebral part: blinking, orbital part: squeezing). Paralysis → patient cannot close the eye (lagophthalmus)

info.o: Fibres from the modiolus and neighbouring mimic muscles
info.i: Skin and mucosa of the lips
info.n: N. facialis (VII) – rr. buccales and marginalis mandibulae
info.f: Closes and purses the lips

info.o: Galea aponeurotica
info.i: Skin of the eyebrows and forehead
info.f: Raises the eyebrows, wrinkles the forehead

info.o: Linea nuchalis suprema and processus mastoideus
info.i: Galea aponeurotica
info.f: Pulls the scalp backwards

info.o: Fascia temporalis above the ear
info.i: Galea aponeurotica
info.f: Tenses the scalp, moves the ear slightly

info.o: Medial end of the arcus superciliaris
info.i: Skin of the middle of the eyebrow
info.f: Pulls the eyebrows medially and down (frowning)

info.o: Os nasale and upper lateral nasal cartilage
info.i: Skin between the eyebrows
info.f: Pulls the skin between the eyebrows down – transverse wrinkles at the root of the nose

info.o: Maxilla above the canine and lateral incisor
info.i: Nasal cartilages and ala nasi
info.f: Narrows (pars transversa) or widens (pars alaris) the nostrils

info.o: Maxilla above the central incisor
info.i: Nasal septum (mobile part)
info.f: Pulls the tip of the nose and septum down

info.o: Infraorbital margin of the maxilla (above the foramen infraorbitale)
info.i: Skin of the upper lip
info.n: N. facialis (VII) – rr. zygomatici and buccales
info.f: Elevates the upper lip

muscles.la: Musculus levator labii superioris alaeque nasi

info.o: Processus frontalis maxillae
info.i: Ala nasi and upper lip
info.f: Elevates the upper lip and widens the nostril

info.o: Fossa canina of the maxilla (below the foramen infraorbitale)
info.i: Angulus oris (modiolus)
info.n: N. facialis (VII) – rr. zygomatici and buccales
info.f: Raises the corner of the mouth

info.o: Lateral surface of the os zygomaticum
info.i: Angulus oris (modiolus)
info.f: Pulls the corner of the mouth up and out – the smiling muscle

info.o: Os zygomaticum, medial to zygomaticus major
info.i: Skin of the upper lip
info.f: Elevates the upper lip (deepens the nasolabial fold)

info.o: Fascia parotidea and masseterica
info.i: Angulus oris
info.f: Pulls the corner of the mouth laterally

info.o: Lower border of the mandible (linea obliqua)
info.i: Angulus oris
info.f: Pulls the corner of the mouth down (sad face)

info.o: Mandible between symphysis and foramen mentale
info.i: Skin of the lower lip
info.f: Pulls the lower lip down and laterally

info.o: Fossa incisiva of the mandible
info.i: Skin of the chin
info.f: Raises and protrudes the lower lip, wrinkles the chin

info.o: Ala minor ossis sphenoidalis, above the canalis opticus
info.i: Upper eyelid (tarsus superior and skin)
info.n: N. oculomotorius (III) – r. superior; its smooth part (M. tarsalis superior) is sympathetic
info.f: Elevates the upper eyelid. Lesion of III → ptosis

info.o: Anulus tendineus communis
info.i: Sclera, superior side
info.f: Elevation (plus adduction and intorsion)

info.o: Anulus tendineus communis
info.i: Sclera, inferior side
info.f: Depression (plus adduction and extorsion)

info.o: Anulus tendineus communis
info.i: Sclera, medial side
info.f: Adduction

info.o: Anulus tendineus communis
info.i: Sclera, lateral side
info.f: Abduction. Lesion of VI → eye turned inwards (convergent squint)

info.o: Body of the sphenoid, above and medial to the canalis opticus
info.i: Sclera posterior-superior-lateral, after running through the trochlea
info.f: Intorsion, depression (most in adduction) and abduction. Lesion of IV → trouble walking downstairs

info.o: Floor of the orbit (maxilla, lateral to the nasolacrimal canal)
info.i: Sclera posterior-inferior-lateral
info.f: Extorsion, elevation (most in adduction) and abduction

info.o: Spina mentalis superior of the mandible
info.i: Whole tongue (fan-shaped) and body of the hyoid
info.f: Protrudes the tongue. Lesion of XII → tongue deviates to the paralysed side

info.o: Body and cornu majus of the hyoid
info.i: Side of the tongue
info.f: Depresses and retracts the tongue

info.o: Skin and fascia of the upper chest (over pectoralis major and deltoid)
info.i: Lower border of the mandible, skin of the lower face and angulus oris
info.f: Tenses the skin of the neck, pulls the corner of the mouth down

info.o: Caput sternale: manubrium sterni · caput claviculare: medial third of the clavicle
info.i: Processus mastoideus and lateral linea nuchalis superior
info.f: One side: tilts the head to the same side and turns the face to the opposite side · both: extend the head, help inspiration. Shortened → torticollis

info.o: Venter posterior: incisura mastoidea · venter anterior: fossa digastrica of the mandible
info.i: Intermediate tendon, held to the hyoid by a fibrous loop
info.n: Venter anterior: n. mylohyoideus (V3) · venter posterior: n. facialis (VII)
info.f: Elevates the hyoid, opens the mouth (depresses the mandible)

info.o: Processus styloideus
info.i: Body of the hyoid (splits around the digastric tendon)
info.f: Elevates and pulls the hyoid backwards (swallowing)

info.o: Linea mylohyoidea of the mandible
info.i: Median raphe and body of the hyoid
info.f: Forms the floor of the mouth, elevates hyoid and tongue, opens the mouth

info.o: Spina mentalis inferior
info.i: Body of the hyoid
info.n: C1 fibres travelling with the n. hypoglossus
info.f: Pulls the hyoid forward and up, opens the mouth

info.o: Back of the manubrium and medial clavicle
info.i: Body of the hyoid
info.f: Depresses the hyoid

info.o: Back of the manubrium (below sternohyoid) and 1st costal cartilage
info.i: Linea obliqua of the thyroid cartilage
info.f: Depresses the larynx

info.o: Linea obliqua of the thyroid cartilage
info.i: Body and cornu majus of the hyoid
info.n: C1 fibres travelling with the n. hypoglossus
info.f: Depresses the hyoid or elevates the larynx

info.o: Venter inferior: upper border of the scapula near the incisura scapulae
info.i: Venter superior: body of the hyoid (intermediate tendon tied to the clavicle)
info.f: Depresses the hyoid, tenses the fascia around the carotid sheath

info.o: Tubercula anteriora C3–C6
info.i: Tuberculum musculi scaleni anterioris of the 1st rib
info.f: Elevates the 1st rib, bends the neck to the side. A. subclavia and plexus brachialis pass behind it through the scalene gap; V. subclavia passes in front

info.o: Tubercula posteriora C2–C7
info.i: 1st rib, behind the sulcus arteriae subclaviae
info.f: Elevates the 1st rib, bends the neck to the side; back wall of the scalene gap

info.o: Tubercula posteriora C5–C7
info.i: Outer surface of the 2nd rib
info.f: Elevates the 2nd rib, bends the neck to the side

info.o: Bodies and transverse processes C3–T3
info.i: Bodies and anterior tubercles C1–C6 (tuberculum anterius atlantis)
info.f: Flexes the cervical spine

info.o: Tubercula anteriora C3–C6
info.i: Pars basilaris of the occipital bone
info.f: Flexes the head and upper neck

info.o: Massa lateralis atlantis
info.i: Pars basilaris of the occipital bone, in front of the foramen magnum
info.f: Flexes the head at the atlanto-occipital joint

info.o: Processus transversus atlantis
info.i: Processus jugularis of the occipital bone
info.f: Bends the head to the side

info.o: Linea nuchalis superior, protuberantia occipitalis externa, lig. nuchae, processus spinosi C7–T12
info.i: Lateral third of the clavicle, acromion, spina scapulae
info.f: Pars descendens elevates, pars transversa retracts, pars ascendens depresses the scapula; together they rotate it upwards (arm above 90°). Lesion of XI → shoulder hangs down

info.o: Processus spinosi T7–L5, fascia thoracolumbalis, crista iliaca, ribs 10–12
info.i: Crista tuberculi minoris humeri
info.f: Adducts, extends and internally rotates the arm (climbing, "hand in back pocket")

info.o: Tubercula posteriora C1–C4
info.i: Angulus superior and upper margo medialis of the scapula
info.f: Elevates the scapula and rotates it downwards

info.o: Processus spinosi T2–T5
info.i: Margo medialis scapulae, below the spine
info.f: Retracts and elevates the scapula, fixes it to the thorax

info.o: Processus spinosi C6–T1
info.i: Margo medialis scapulae, at the root of the spine
info.f: Retracts and elevates the scapula

info.o: Processus spinosi C6–T2
info.i: Ribs 2–5, lateral to their angles
info.f: Elevates the ribs (inspiration)

info.o: Processus spinosi T11–L2, fascia thoracolumbalis
info.i: Lower borders of ribs 9–12
info.f: Pulls the lower ribs down

info.o: Lig. nuchae, processus spinosi C7–T3
info.i: Processus mastoideus, lateral linea nuchalis superior
info.f: Both sides: extend the head · one side: turns and bends the head to the same side

info.o: Processus spinosi T3–T6
info.i: Tubercula posteriora C1–C3
info.f: Extends the neck, turns it to the same side

info.o: Sacrum, crista iliaca, fascia thoracolumbalis
info.i: Angles of ribs 5–12
info.f: Extends the spine, bends it to the same side (lateral tract of the erector spinae)

info.o: Angles of ribs 7–12
info.i: Angles of ribs 1–6 and processus transversus C7
info.f: Extends the thoracic spine, bends it to the same side

info.o: Angles of ribs 3–6
info.i: Tubercula posteriora C4–C6
info.f: Extends the neck, bends it to the same side

info.o: Sacrum, processus spinosi of the lumbar vertebrae, lower thoracic transverse processes
info.i: Processus costales/transversi of lumbar and thoracic vertebrae, ribs 2–12
info.f: Extends the spine, bends it to the same side

info.o: Processus transversi T1–T6
info.i: Tubercula posteriora C2–C5
info.f: Extends the neck, bends it to the same side

info.o: Processus transversi T1–T3 and articular processes C4–C7
info.i: Processus mastoideus
info.f: Extends the head, turns and bends it to the same side

info.o: Processus spinosi T10–L2
info.i: Processus spinosi T2–T8
info.f: Extends the thoracic spine (medial tract)

info.o: Processus spinosi C6–T2
info.i: Processus spinosi C2–C4
info.f: Extends the neck

info.o: Processus spinosi C7–T3 (inconstant)
info.i: Occipital bone near the protuberantia occipitalis externa
info.f: Extends the head

info.o: Processus transversi T7–T12
info.i: Processus spinosi C6–T4 (spans 5–6 segments)
info.f: Extends the spine and turns it to the opposite side

info.o: Processus transversi T1–T6
info.i: Processus spinosi C2–C5
info.f: Extends the neck and turns it to the opposite side

info.o: Sacrum, mamillary processes (lumbar), transverse processes (thoracic), articular processes C4–C7
info.i: Processus spinosi 2–4 segments higher, up to C2
info.f: Stabilises the vertebrae, extends and turns the spine to the opposite side

info.o: Processus transversi
info.i: Lamina and base of the spinous process 1–2 vertebrae higher
info.f: Turn the spine to the opposite side; proprioception

info.o: Processus spinosus of one vertebra
info.i: Processus spinosus of the vertebra above
info.f: Extend the spine (mainly cervical and lumbar)

parts: Dorsal parts of lateral intertransversarii lumborum muscles
Ventral parts of lateral intertransversarii lumborum muscles

info.o: Processus costalis of one lumbar vertebra
info.i: Processus costalis of the vertebra above
info.f: Bend the lumbar spine to the side

info.o: Processus transversi C7–T11
info.i: Next lower rib (breves) or the second rib below (longi)
info.f: Elevate the ribs, bend and turn the spine

info.o: Processus spinosus axis
info.i: Middle part of the linea nuchalis inferior
info.f: Extends the head and turns it to the same side

info.o: Tuberculum posterius atlantis
info.i: Medial part of the linea nuchalis inferior
info.f: Extends the head

info.o: Processus spinosus axis
info.i: Processus transversus atlantis
info.f: Turns atlas and head to the same side

info.o: Processus transversus atlantis
info.i: Lateral part of the linea nuchalis inferior
info.f: Extends the head and bends it to the same side

parts: Clavicular head of pectoralis major muscle
Sternocostal head of pectoralis major muscle

info.o: Pars clavicularis: medial half of the clavicle · pars sternocostalis: sternum and costal cartilages 1–6 · pars abdominalis: rectus sheath
info.i: Crista tuberculi majoris humeri
info.f: Adducts and internally rotates the arm, clavicular part flexes it; accessory inspiratory muscle

info.o: Ribs 3–5
info.i: Processus coracoideus
info.f: Pulls the scapula forward and down; accessory inspiratory muscle

info.o: 1st rib at the bone–cartilage junction
info.i: Lower surface of the lateral clavicle
info.f: Stabilises the sternoclavicular joint, pulls the clavicle down

info.o: Ribs 1–9 (digitations on the outer surface)
info.i: Margo medialis scapulae (costal side), angulus superior and inferior
info.f: Pulls the scapula forward, rotates it upwards (arm above 90°), holds it against the thorax. Lesion → scapula alata

info.o: Lower border of the rib above
info.i: Upper border of the rib below (fibres run down and forward – "hands in pockets")
info.f: Elevate the ribs – inspiration

info.o: Upper border of the rib below
info.i: Lower border of the rib above (fibres run down and backward)
info.f: Depress the ribs – expiration (parasternal part helps inspiration)

info.o: Upper border of the rib below
info.i: Lower border of the rib above (deepest layer)
info.f: Like the internal intercostals; the intercostal vein, artery and nerve (VAN) run between interni and intimi

info.o: Back of the lower sternum and processus xiphoideus
info.i: Costal cartilages 2–6
info.f: Pulls the costal cartilages down – expiration

info.o: Pars sternalis: processus xiphoideus · pars costalis: costal cartilages 7–12 · pars lumbalis: crura on L1–L3 and ligg. arcuata
info.i: Centrum tendineum
info.n: N. phrenicus (C3–C5) – "C3, 4, 5 keeps the diaphragm alive"
info.f: Main inspiratory muscle. Openings: V. cava T8, oesophagus T10, aorta T12

info.o: Crista pubica and symphysis pubica
info.i: Costal cartilages 5–7 and processus xiphoideus
info.f: Flexes the trunk, abdominal press; tendinous intersections make the "six-pack"

info.o: Outer surface of ribs 5–12
info.i: Labium externum of the crista iliaca, lig. inguinale, aponeurosis to the linea alba
info.n: Nn. intercostales T5–T11, n. subcostalis, n. iliohypogastricus
info.f: One side: turns the trunk to the opposite side, bends it to the same side · both: flex the trunk, abdominal press

info.o: Fascia thoracolumbalis, linea intermedia of the crista iliaca, lateral lig. inguinale
info.i: Lower borders of ribs 10–12, aponeurosis to the linea alba; gives the M. cremaster
info.n: Nn. intercostales T8–T11, n. subcostalis, nn. iliohypogastricus and ilioinguinalis
info.f: One side: turns the trunk to the same side · both: flex the trunk, abdominal press

info.o: Inner surface of costal cartilages 7–12, fascia thoracolumbalis, labium internum of the crista iliaca, lateral lig. inguinale
info.i: Aponeurosis to the linea alba
info.n: Nn. intercostales T7–T11, n. subcostalis, nn. iliohypogastricus and ilioinguinalis
info.f: Abdominal press, narrows the waist like a belt

info.o: Ramus superior ossis pubis, in front of rectus abdominis
info.i: Linea alba
info.f: Tenses the linea alba (often absent)

info.o: Labium internum of the crista iliaca, lig. iliolumbale
info.i: 12th rib and processus costales L1–L4
info.n: N. subcostalis (T12) and rr. anteriores L1–L4
info.f: Bends the trunk to the side, holds the 12th rib down during inspiration

info.o: Bodies and discs T12–L4, processus costales L1–L5
info.i: Trochanter minor (together with iliacus as M. iliopsoas)
info.n: Rr. musculares of the plexus lumbalis (L1–L3)
info.f: Strongest hip flexor, also external rotation; bends the lumbar spine

parts: Scapular spinal part of deltoid muscle

info.o: Lateral third of the clavicle, acromion, spina scapulae
info.i: Tuberositas deltoidea humeri
info.f: Pars acromialis abducts the arm (15–90°), pars clavicularis flexes and rotates inwards, pars spinalis extends and rotates outwards. Fracture of the surgical neck → axillary nerve at risk

info.o: Fossa supraspinata
info.i: Upper facet of the tuberculum majus
info.f: Starts abduction (first 15°); rotator cuff. Most often torn cuff tendon (painful arc)

info.o: Fossa infraspinata
info.i: Middle facet of the tuberculum majus
info.f: External rotation; rotator cuff

info.o: Margo lateralis scapulae (upper part)
info.i: Lower facet of the tuberculum majus
info.f: External rotation; rotator cuff

info.o: Fossa subscapularis
info.i: Tuberculum minus
info.f: Internal rotation; rotator cuff

info.o: Angulus inferior scapulae
info.i: Crista tuberculi minoris
info.f: Adduction, extension and internal rotation of the arm

info.o: Processus coracoideus
info.i: Medial shaft of the humerus (middle)
info.n: N. musculocutaneus (C6–C7) – it pierces the muscle
info.f: Flexes and adducts the arm

info.o: Caput longum: tuberculum supraglenoidale · caput breve: processus coracoideus
info.i: Tuberositas radii and aponeurosis bicipitalis
info.f: Flexes the elbow, strongest supinator (elbow bent), helps flex the shoulder. Biceps reflex C5–C6

info.o: Anterior surface of the distal half of the humerus
info.i: Tuberositas ulnae
info.n: N. musculocutaneus (small lateral part: n. radialis)
info.f: Pure, strongest elbow flexor

info.o: Caput longum: tuberculum infraglenoidale · caput laterale: humerus above the sulcus n. radialis · caput mediale: humerus below it
info.i: Olecranon
info.f: Extends the elbow; long head also extends and adducts the arm. Triceps reflex C7

info.o: Epicondylus lateralis humeri
info.i: Lateral surface of the olecranon
info.f: Helps extend the elbow, tenses the joint capsule

info.o: Caput humerale: epicondylus medialis · caput ulnare: processus coronoideus ulnae
info.i: Lateral surface of the middle radius
info.n: N. medianus (C6–C7) – runs between the two heads
info.f: Pronation, helps flex the elbow

info.o: Epicondylus medialis humeri
info.i: Base of the 2nd metacarpal (palmar)
info.f: Flexes the wrist and abducts it radially

info.o: Epicondylus medialis humeri
info.i: Aponeurosis palmaris
info.f: Tenses the palmar aponeurosis, helps flex the wrist; missing in about 15 %

parts: Humeral head of flexor carpi ulnaris
Ulnar head of flexor carpi ulnaris

info.o: Epicondylus medialis · olecranon and posterior border of the ulna
info.i: Os pisiforme (→ hamulus ossis hamati, base of MC 5)
info.f: Flexes the wrist and abducts it to the ulnar side

parts: Humero-ulnar head of flexor digitorum superficialis
Radial head of flexor digitorum superficialis

info.o: Epicondylus medialis, processus coronoideus ulnae, anterior radius
info.i: Middle phalanges of fingers 2–5 (split tendons)
info.f: Flexes the PIP joints (and MCP and wrist)

info.o: Anterior surface of the ulna and membrana interossea
info.i: Distal phalanges of fingers 2–5 (through the split FDS tendons)
info.n: Radial half (fingers 2–3): n. interosseus anterior (n. medianus) · ulnar half (4–5): n. ulnaris
info.f: Flexes the DIP joints – only muscle that bends the fingertip

info.o: Anterior surface of the radius and membrana interossea
info.i: Distal phalanx of the thumb
info.f: Flexes the thumb tip (IP joint)

info.o: Distal anterior surface of the ulna
info.i: Distal anterior surface of the radius
info.f: Main pronator

info.o: Lateral supracondylar ridge of the humerus
info.i: Processus styloideus radii
info.f: Flexes the elbow in mid-position ("beer-drinking muscle")

info.o: Lateral supracondylar ridge of the humerus
info.i: Base of the 2nd metacarpal (dorsal)
info.f: Extends the wrist and abducts it radially (fist clenching)

info.o: Epicondylus lateralis humeri
info.i: Base of the 3rd metacarpal (dorsal)
info.f: Extends the wrist. Its origin is the classic site of tennis elbow

info.o: Epicondylus lateralis humeri
info.i: Dorsal aponeurosis of fingers 2–5
info.n: N. interosseus posterior (r. profundus n. radialis, C7–C8)
info.f: Extends the fingers and the wrist

info.o: Epicondylus lateralis humeri
info.i: Dorsal aponeurosis of the little finger
info.n: N. interosseus posterior (r. profundus n. radialis, C7–C8)
info.f: Extends the little finger

parts: Humeral head of extensor carpi ulnaris
Ulnar head of extensor carpi ulnaris

info.o: Epicondylus lateralis · posterior border of the ulna
info.i: Base of the 5th metacarpal (dorsal)
info.n: N. interosseus posterior (r. profundus n. radialis, C7–C8)
info.f: Extends the wrist and abducts it to the ulnar side

info.o: Epicondylus lateralis, lig. collaterale radiale and anulare, crista m. supinatoris ulnae
info.i: Proximal radius (around the neck and shaft)
info.n: R. profundus n. radialis (C6–C7) – runs through it
info.f: Supination (with the elbow straight)

info.o: Posterior surfaces of ulna and radius, membrana interossea
info.i: Base of the 1st metacarpal
info.n: N. interosseus posterior (r. profundus n. radialis, C7–C8)
info.f: Abducts the thumb, helps radial abduction of the wrist

info.o: Posterior surface of the radius and membrana interossea
info.i: Proximal phalanx of the thumb
info.n: N. interosseus posterior (r. profundus n. radialis, C7–C8)
info.f: Extends the thumb MCP joint; borders the anatomical snuffbox

info.o: Posterior surface of the ulna and membrana interossea
info.i: Distal phalanx of the thumb (around the tuberculum dorsale radii)
info.n: N. interosseus posterior (r. profundus n. radialis, C7–C8)
info.f: Extends the thumb IP joint; ulnar border of the snuffbox

info.o: Distal posterior surface of the ulna
info.i: Dorsal aponeurosis of the index finger
info.n: N. interosseus posterior (r. profundus n. radialis, C7–C8)
info.f: Extends the index finger (pointing)

info.o: Retinaculum musculorum flexorum, tuberculum ossis scaphoidei
info.i: Proximal phalanx of the thumb (radial sesamoid)
info.f: Abducts the thumb. Wasting of the thenar → carpal tunnel syndrome

parts: Superficial head of flexor pollicis brevis
Deep head of flexor pollicis brevis

info.o: Caput superficiale: retinaculum flexorum · caput profundum: trapezoideum, capitatum
info.i: Proximal phalanx of the thumb (radial sesamoid)
info.n: Caput superficiale: n. medianus · caput profundum: n. ulnaris
info.f: Flexes the thumb MCP joint

info.o: Retinaculum flexorum, tuberculum ossis trapezii
info.i: Radial border of the 1st metacarpal
info.f: Opposition of the thumb

info.o: Caput obliquum: capitatum, bases of MC 2–3 · caput transversum: palmar shaft of MC 3
info.i: Proximal phalanx of the thumb (ulnar sesamoid)
info.f: Adducts the thumb. Weak → Froment sign

info.o: Os pisiforme
info.i: Proximal phalanx of the little finger (ulnar side)
info.f: Abducts the little finger

info.o: Hamulus ossis hamati, retinaculum flexorum
info.i: Proximal phalanx of the little finger
info.f: Flexes the little finger at the MCP joint

parts: Opponens digiti minimi muscle of hand

info.o: Hamulus ossis hamati, retinaculum flexorum
info.i: Ulnar border of the 5th metacarpal
info.f: Brings the 5th metacarpal towards the thumb

info.o: Tendons of flexor digitorum profundus
info.i: Radial side of the dorsal aponeurosis of fingers 2–5
info.f: Flex the MCP joints and extend the IP joints

info.o: Metacarpals 2, 4, 5 (side facing the middle finger)
info.i: Dorsal aponeurosis of fingers 2, 4, 5
info.f: Adduct the fingers (PAD), flex MCP, extend IP

info.o: Adjacent sides of metacarpals 1–5 (two heads)
info.i: Proximal phalanges and dorsal aponeurosis of fingers 2–4
info.f: Abduct the fingers (DAB), flex MCP, extend IP

regions.title: Lower limb – hip, thigh, leg, foot

info.o: Fossa iliaca
info.i: Trochanter minor (with psoas major as M. iliopsoas)
info.f: Strongest hip flexor (as iliopsoas)

info.o: Bodies and discs T12–L4, processus costales L1–L5
info.i: Trochanter minor
info.n: Rr. musculares of the plexus lumbalis (L1–L3)
info.f: Flexes the hip (iliopsoas), bends the lumbar spine

info.o: Posterior ilium, sacrum, coccyx, lig. sacrotuberale
info.i: Tuberositas glutea and tractus iliotibialis
info.f: Strongest hip extensor and external rotator (climbing stairs, standing up)

info.o: Outer surface of the ilium between the anterior and posterior gluteal lines
info.i: Lateral surface of the trochanter major
info.f: Abducts the hip and keeps the pelvis level when standing on one leg. Weak → Trendelenburg sign

info.o: Outer surface of the ilium between the anterior and inferior gluteal lines
info.i: Anterior surface of the trochanter major
info.f: Abducts and internally rotates the hip, stabilises the pelvis

info.o: Spina iliaca anterior superior
info.i: Tractus iliotibialis → tuberculum of the lateral tibia (Gerdy)
info.f: Flexes, abducts and internally rotates the hip; tenses the iliotibial tract

info.o: Anterior (pelvic) surface of the sacrum
info.i: Tip of the trochanter major
info.f: External rotation and abduction; divides the greater sciatic foramen into supra- and infrapiriform foramen

info.o: Inner surface of the membrana obturatoria and the bone around it
info.i: Fossa trochanterica
info.f: External rotation; leaves the pelvis through the lesser sciatic foramen

info.o: Spina ischiadica
info.i: With the obturator internus tendon to the fossa trochanterica
info.f: External rotation

info.o: Tuber ischiadicum
info.i: With the obturator internus tendon to the fossa trochanterica
info.f: External rotation

info.o: Lateral border of the tuber ischiadicum
info.i: Crista intertrochanterica
info.f: External rotation and adduction

info.o: Outer surface of the membrana obturatoria and the bone around it
info.i: Fossa trochanterica
info.f: External rotation and adduction

info.o: Spina iliaca anterior superior
info.i: Pes anserinus superficialis (medial tibia)
info.f: Flexes, abducts and externally rotates the hip; flexes the knee (tailor’s position)

info.o: Spina iliaca anterior inferior and upper rim of the acetabulum
info.i: Tuberositas tibiae via the patella and lig. patellae
info.f: Extends the knee and flexes the hip (only two-joint head of the quadriceps). Patellar reflex L3–L4

info.o: Trochanter major, labium laterale lineae asperae
info.i: Tuberositas tibiae via patella and lig. patellae, lateral retinaculum
info.f: Extends the knee

info.o: Linea intertrochanterica, labium mediale lineae asperae
info.i: Tuberositas tibiae via patella and lig. patellae, medial retinaculum
info.f: Extends the knee, keeps the patella from slipping laterally

info.o: Anterior and lateral surface of the femoral shaft
info.i: Tuberositas tibiae via patella and lig. patellae
info.f: Extends the knee

info.o: Pecten ossis pubis
info.i: Linea pectinea femoris
info.f: Adducts and flexes the hip

info.o: Ramus superior ossis pubis, below the crista pubica
info.i: Middle third of the labium mediale lineae asperae
info.f: Adducts and flexes the hip

info.o: Ramus inferior ossis pubis
info.i: Upper third of the linea aspera
info.f: Adducts the hip

info.o: Ramus inferior ossis pubis, ramus ossis ischii, tuber ischiadicum
info.i: Linea aspera and tuberculum adductorium
info.n: N. obturatorius + tibial part of the n. ischiadicus (L2–L5)
info.f: Strongest adductor, also extends the hip; the hiatus adductorius lets the femoral vessels into the popliteal fossa

info.o: Ramus inferior ossis pubis
info.i: Pes anserinus superficialis (medial tibia)
info.f: Adducts the hip, flexes and internally rotates the knee

info.o: Caput longum: tuber ischiadicum · caput breve: labium laterale lineae asperae
info.i: Caput fibulae
info.n: Caput longum: n. tibialis part · caput breve: n. fibularis communis part of the n. ischiadicus
info.f: Flexes and externally rotates the knee; long head extends the hip

info.o: Tuber ischiadicum
info.i: Pes anserinus superficialis (medial tibia)
info.n: N. tibialis part of the n. ischiadicus (L5–S2)
info.f: Extends the hip, flexes and internally rotates the knee

info.o: Tuber ischiadicum
info.i: Posterior medial condyle of the tibia (pes anserinus profundus), lig. popliteum obliquum
info.n: N. tibialis part of the n. ischiadicus (L5–S2)
info.f: Extends the hip, flexes and internally rotates the knee

info.o: Lateral surface of the tibia, membrana interossea
info.i: Os cuneiforme mediale and base of MT 1 (plantar)
info.f: Dorsiflexion and inversion (supination). Paralysis → foot drop, steppage gait

info.o: Condylus lateralis tibiae, fibula, membrana interossea
info.i: Dorsal aponeurosis of toes 2–5
info.f: Extends the toes, dorsiflexion and eversion

info.o: Medial surface of the fibula, membrana interossea
info.i: Distal phalanx of the big toe
info.f: Extends the big toe, dorsiflexion. Weak big-toe extension → L5 root

info.o: Distal anterior fibula
info.i: Base of MT 5 (dorsal)
info.f: Dorsiflexion and eversion

info.o: Caput fibulae and proximal lateral fibula
info.i: Os cuneiforme mediale and base of MT 1 (crosses the sole)
info.f: Eversion (pronation), plantar flexion, supports the transverse arch

info.o: Distal lateral fibula
info.i: Tuberositas ossis metatarsi quinti
info.f: Eversion and plantar flexion

info.o: Caput mediale: condylus medialis femoris · caput laterale: condylus lateralis femoris
info.i: Tuber calcanei via the tendo calcaneus (Achilles)
info.f: Plantar flexion, flexes the knee. Achilles reflex S1

info.o: Caput and posterior fibula, linea musculi solei tibiae, arcus tendineus
info.i: Tuber calcanei via the tendo calcaneus
info.f: Plantar flexion, keeps you upright when standing; muscle pump for the veins

info.o: Femur above the condylus lateralis
info.i: Tuber calcanei (medial to the Achilles tendon)
info.f: Weak plantar flexion and knee flexion

info.o: Condylus lateralis femoris, lateral meniscus
info.i: Posterior tibia above the linea musculi solei
info.f: "Unlocks" the extended knee by rotating the tibia inwards

info.o: Membrana interossea, posterior tibia and fibula
info.i: Tuberositas ossis navicularis, cuneiforms, bases of MT 2–4
info.f: Inversion and plantar flexion; holds up the longitudinal arch

info.o: Posterior surface of the tibia
info.i: Distal phalanges of toes 2–5
info.f: Flexes the toes, plantar flexion and inversion

info.o: Posterior surface of the fibula, membrana interossea
info.i: Distal phalanx of the big toe
info.f: Flexes the big toe – push-off when walking

info.o: Dorsal surface of the calcaneus
info.i: Dorsal aponeurosis of toes 2–4
info.f: Extends toes 2–4

info.o: Dorsal surface of the calcaneus
info.i: Proximal phalanx of the big toe
info.f: Extends the big toe at the MTP joint

info.o: Processus medialis tuberis calcanei, retinaculum flexorum
info.i: Proximal phalanx of the big toe (medial sesamoid)
info.f: Abducts and flexes the big toe, supports the medial arch

parts: Medial head of flexor hallucis brevis
Lateral head of flexor hallucis brevis

info.o: Plantar surface of the cuboid and cuneiforms
info.i: Proximal phalanx of the big toe (both sesamoids)
info.n: Caput mediale: n. plantaris medialis · caput laterale: n. plantaris lateralis
info.f: Flexes the big toe at the MTP joint

info.o: Caput obliquum: bases of MT 2–4, cuboid · caput transversum: MTP joint capsules 3–5
info.i: Proximal phalanx of the big toe (lateral sesamoid)
info.f: Adducts the big toe, supports the transverse arch

info.o: Tuber calcanei, aponeurosis plantaris
info.i: Middle phalanges of toes 2–5
info.f: Flexes the PIP joints of the toes

info.o: Plantar surface of the calcaneus (two heads)
info.i: Lateral border of the flexor digitorum longus tendon
info.f: Straightens the pull of flexor digitorum longus

info.o: Tuber calcanei
info.i: Proximal phalanx of the 5th toe (lateral)
info.f: Abducts and flexes the 5th toe, supports the lateral arch

muscles.la: Musculus flexor digiti minimi brevis pedis

info.o: Base of MT 5, lig. plantare longum
info.i: Proximal phalanx of the 5th toe
info.f: Flexes the 5th toe at the MTP joint

info.o: Tendons of flexor digitorum longus
info.i: Medial side of the dorsal aponeurosis of toes 2–5
info.n: 1st: n. plantaris medialis · 2nd–4th: n. plantaris lateralis
info.f: Flex the MTP joints, extend the IP joints

info.o: Medial side of MT 3–5
info.i: Proximal phalanges of toes 3–5 (medial)
info.f: Adduct toes 3–5 towards the 2nd toe

info.o: Adjacent sides of MT 1–5 (two heads)
info.i: Proximal phalanges of toes 2–4
info.f: Abduct the toes away from the axis of the 2nd toe
